intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming the open plains with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a backdrop. Amboseli is renowned for its large tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities at close range in a relatively compact park.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track both black and white rhinos on foot or by vehicle at Ol Pejeta, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. The conservancy also shelters chimpanzees, lions, and wild dogs. A guided walking safari with armed rangers provides an intimate and thrilling wildlife experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its millions of pink flamingos lining the alkaline lake shores. The park also hosts Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and over 450 bird species, making it a paradise for birdwatchers and nature photographers.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Visit an authentic Maasai village near the Mara to learn about traditional customs, warrior jumping dances, beadwork, and medicinal plant knowledge. Cap the experience with a bush dinner under the stars on the open savannah, listening to wildlife sounds while enjoying traditional Kenyan cuisine including nyama choma and ugali.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange budget airport transfer (matatu or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with the resort surroundings and nearby beachfront area.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely sunset stroll along the beachfront to decompress after travel. Explore the immediate shoreline, watch local fishermen return with their catch, and soak in the warm coastal atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick affordable bite at the airport - look for local snack stalls or budget cafeteria options (approx. KES 300-500)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's most affordable dining option or a nearby local restaurant serving Swahili coastal cuisine such as ugali, sukuma wiki, and grilled fish (approx. KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel and arrival day. Keep the evening light to recover from the flight. Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates and grab a local SIM card for affordable data. Warm summer weather expected with highs around 25°C - perfect for settling in.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk along the beachfront to watch the sunrise over the Indian Ocean. Explore the tidal pools and observe coastal birdlife including herons, kingfishers, and wading birds. This free activity is ideal for wildlife enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market to experience authentic Kenyan coastal culture and pick up affordable fresh fruits, snacks, and souvenirs. Spend time exploring the surrounding nature trails or mangrove areas accessible from the resort area on foot or by tuk-tuk.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a budget-friendly local cultural evening if available near the resort, or relax on the beach and stargaze. Chat with local guides about upcoming safari options to plan the rest of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruits and mandazi (Kenyan fried dough) from a local vendor near the beach (approx. KES 200-300)
meals.lunch: Local coastal restaurant - try a plate of rice, beans, and grilled tilapia or calamari (approx. KES 400-600)
meals.dinner: Street food evening - nyama choma (grilled meat) with kachumbari salad from a local roadside grill (approx. KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Begin researching and booking your safari day trips in advance to secure the best budget rates. Temperatures will be comfortable around 25°C. Apply sunscreen and stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group day safari tour departing early morning to a nearby wildlife conservancy or national park accessible from the coastal region. Look for affordable shared group tours which significantly reduce costs. Spot wildlife including zebras, giraffes, and various antelope species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the safari game drive through the afternoon, enjoying picnic lunch inside the park. Look out for elephants, buffaloes, and an abundance of birdlife. July is excellent for wildlife viewing as animals gather around water sources.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Rest and recover from the safari. Share photos and experiences with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early morning light breakfast at the resort or packed snacks before departure (approx. KES 300-400)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch prepared affordably before departure or included in the group safari package - sandwiches, fruits, and water
meals.dinner: Back at the resort area, enjoy a hearty local meal at a budget eatery - chicken stew with ugali and vegetables (approx. KES 600-800)

day_by_day.notes: Book group safari tours rather than private ones to cut costs significantly. Bring binoculars, a camera, sunscreen, and a light jacket for early morning game drives. July is dry season making wildlife viewing exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local coastal nature on a self-guided walking trail or hire a local nature guide for a budget-friendly walking tour of coastal forest and mangrove ecosystems. Look for monkeys, exotic birds, and unique coastal flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local community conservation project or wildlife rescue center near the coast. Many offer affordable entry fees and provide insight into Kenya's conservation efforts. Great opportunity to learn about local wildlife rehabilitation.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dhow cruise along the coastline - a quintessential Kenyan coastal experience. Look for budget group dhow rides which are very affordable and offer beautiful views of the coastline and potential dolphin sightings.

meals.breakfast: Swahili breakfast at a local cafe - chai tea, mahamri (coconut doughnuts), and eggs (approx. KES 250-350)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local beach shack - grilled prawns or octopus with rice and coconut sauce (approx. KES 500-700)
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at a budget local restaurant - pilau rice with spiced meat or vegetarian curry (approx. KES 600-800)

day_by_day.notes: Hire local guides rather than agency guides to save money and support the community directly. Negotiate prices politely but fairly. Carry insect repellent for evening activities near the water.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day budget safari excursion - depart early for a longer safari journey to a more distant wildlife area or national reserve. This is a great opportunity to see the Big Five if the conservancy is nearby. Enjoy the dramatic Kenyan landscape at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive continuing through the reserve. Peak afternoon hours often bring predator activity. Look for lions, leopards, cheetahs, and large elephant herds gathering near waterholes during the dry July season.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort. Stop at a local town along the way for an authentic budget dinner experience before arriving back at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast - packed bread, peanut butter, and fruit before departure (approx. KES 150-200)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or affordable park canteen meal - sandwiches and fresh juice (approx. KES 400-500)
meals.dinner: Local town restaurant on the return journey - githeri (corn and beans stew) or nyama choma with chapati (approx. KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: This is likely the highlight safari day. Ensure camera batteries are fully charged. Wear neutral colored clothing - khaki, olive, or beige - for best wildlife viewing etiquette. Carry sufficient water for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and spend time on the beach. Take a morning swim in the warm Indian Ocean waters and relax. This is a well-earned rest day after two intensive safari days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot or by affordable tuk-tuk. Visit a local school or community project if open to visitors, or spend time at a nearby nature trail observing coastal birdlife and butterflies.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local cooking class if available affordably nearby, learning to prepare traditional Swahili dishes. This is a great cultural and culinary experience that doubles as entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or fresh tropical fruit platter from a local vendor - mango, papaya, pineapple (approx. KES 300-400)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch - fresh coconut, samosas, and bhajias from a local vendor (approx. KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner if enrolled, or local Swahili restaurant - biryani rice with spiced lamb or chicken (approx. KES 700-900)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important to recharge energy. Use this day to review remaining budget, re-book any remaining safari activities, and do laundry if needed. Check weather forecast for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching excursion. Kenya is a world-class birdwatching destination with over 1,000 species. Hire a local birding guide for a budget-friendly 3-hour morning walk. Look for hornbills, sunbirds, fish eagles, and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local nature reserve or protected forest area accessible by matatu from the resort area. Explore walking trails through indigenous coastal forest and observe wildlife including bushbabies, small antelopes, and exotic reptiles.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the beach for sunset. Engage with local fishermen and learn about traditional fishing techniques. Purchase fresh fish directly from fishermen for a very affordable self-catered beach barbecue experience.

meals.breakfast: Early birdwatching breakfast - packed mandazi and thermos of chai tea (approx. KES 150-200)
meals.lunch: Affordable local canteen near the forest reserve - rice and beans with vegetable stew (approx. KES 350-450)
meals.dinner: Self-catered beach barbecue with fresh fish purchased from local fishermen - extremely affordable and memorable (approx. KES 400-600 for fresh fish and charcoal)

day_by_day.notes: Birdwatching is free or very low cost but incredibly rewarding in Kenya. Bring a field guide or download a free bird identification app before the trip. Morning hours between 6am-9am are the best for bird activity.

day_by_day.morning: Take an affordable matatu or local bus to explore a nearby town or village. Visit the local market, interact with artisans, and observe daily Kenyan life. This cultural immersion experience is completely free and highly enriching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the coastal area and spend the afternoon snorkeling or exploring tidal reef areas. The warm July waters are crystal clear and teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and colorful coral. Rent basic snorkel gear affordably from local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening out - enjoy a special but still budget-friendly dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant to celebrate a wonderful trip. Explore the beachfront night scene and enjoy live local music if available.

meals.breakfast: Local town breakfast on arrival - chai and mandazi or chapati with eggs at a small local cafe (approx. KES 200-300)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in town - samosas, roasted corn, and fresh sugarcane juice (approx. KES 200-300)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated budget dinner - whole grilled snapper with coconut rice and fresh salad at a beachfront restaurant (approx. KES 800-1200)

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling equipment can often be rented very cheaply from beach vendors. Always check reef conditions before entering the water. Be respectful when visiting local villages and always ask permission before photographing people.

day_by_day.morning: Final safari or nature experience - book a budget morning game walk or guided nature trail in a nearby conservancy. Walking safaris offer an intimate wildlife experience and are often more affordable than vehicle game drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing at the beach, swimming, and reflecting on the trip. Visit any local spots you may have missed during the previous days. Purchase any final souvenirs from local artisans - support local craft makers directly.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach bonfire or gathering with fellow travelers and local friends made during the trip. Share stories and experiences. Pack bags and prepare for departure the following day.

meals.breakfast: Full resort or local breakfast to fuel the morning walk - eggs, toast, fresh juice, and chai (approx. KES 400-500)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch - grilled corn, fresh coconut, and a plate of chips with kachumbari (approx. KES 300-450)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip - a comforting familiar meal to end the journey (approx. KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris require closed-toe shoes and are conducted with armed rangers for safety. This is a deeply immersive wildlife experience. Use the afternoon to ensure all packing is done and confirm airport transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk to say goodbye to the Kenyan coastline. Collect any remaining belongings, check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort, and arrange affordable shared shuttle or matatu transfer to the airport. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure procedures - check in, clear security, and browse duty-free shops for any last-minute affordable Kenyan souvenirs such as locally made coffee, tea, or small crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days of wildlife, safari, nature, and authentic Kenyan coastal culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast before checkout - fresh tropical fruits, chai, and mandazi (approx. KES 300-400)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or snacks - budget airport cafeteria or bring snacks purchased locally (approx. KES 400-600)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flight check-in. Keep some Kenyan shillings for any last-minute tips or small purchases. Total estimated daily food budget throughout the trip: KES 1,500-2,500 per day (approximately USD 10-17). Safari day trips can range from KES 3,000-8,000 per person when booked as group tours.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Nairobi to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 1–2 hours depending on location). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to orient yourself and enjoy the warm July weather.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach followed by a welcome dinner at the resort restaurant. Enjoy fresh Kenyan coastal cuisine including grilled tilapia or nyama choma (roasted meat) paired with ugali.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at the airport or during transfer
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — budget approx. KES 2,000–3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it relaxed. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings with the concierge. Hydrate well after the flight. Average high of 25°C makes the evening walk very pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk along the resort's coastal trail or nearby nature reserve. Spot local birdlife and enjoy the crisp morning air before the day heats up. Ideal time for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or cultural center to pick up Maasai crafts, kikoi fabrics, and handmade jewelry. Get acquainted with Kenyan culture and stock up on essentials for safari days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sundowners at the resort bar overlooking the ocean, followed by dinner featuring Swahili-inspired dishes such as pilau rice, coconut fish curry, or kachumbari salad.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — included or approx. KES 1,200
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café near the market — approx. KES 800–1,200
meals.dinner: Swahili cuisine dinner at the resort or a nearby mid-range restaurant — approx. KES 2,000–3,000

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recover from jet lag and prepare for the safari circuit. Pack safari bags lightly — most bush camps have strict luggage weight limits of 15 kg for small aircraft transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by road or scheduled domestic flight to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 3–4 hours by road from Nairobi area or 45 min by flight). Check in at a mid-range lodge inside or near the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — embark on an afternoon game drive around Lake Nakuru, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Marvel at millions of pink flamingos carpeting the lake's shoreline, spot white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, lions, and over 450 bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge for dinner. Enjoy a campfire under the stars with fellow travelers. Listen to the sounds of the African bush as night falls.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a local restaurant en route — approx. KES 800–1,500
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lake Nakuru lodge — approx. KES 2,500–4,000 or included in lodge package

day_by_day.notes: July is peak dry season around Nakuru — excellent visibility for wildlife. Bring binoculars for flamingo and bird watching. Sunscreen and a light jacket for evenings are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park. Focus on tracking the park's famous black and white rhinos, leopards resting in acacia trees, and large buffalo herds near the lake's southern shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lake Nakuru and transfer to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approx. 2.5 hours). Check in at a mid-range tented camp or lodge within or adjacent to the conservancy.
day_by_day.evening: Evening game drive at Ol Pejeta Conservancy. Spot lions, cheetahs, and elephants as the golden hour light creates stunning photographic opportunities across the open savannah.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge — included or approx. KES 1,000
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during transfer or light meal at a roadside café
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta lodge or tented camp — approx. KES 2,500–4,500

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — Najin and Fatu. This is a historically significant wildlife experience. Photography strictly regulated near the rhinos.

day_by_day.morning: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — join a guided rhino tracking experience on foot or by vehicle. A knowledgeable ranger will lead you to both black and white rhinos, sharing conservation stories about the critically endangered northern white rhino subspecies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ol Pejeta chimpanzee sanctuary — the only place in Kenya where you can see rescued chimpanzees. Explore the conservancy's educational center to learn about anti-poaching efforts and wildlife conservation initiatives.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the open plains followed by a bush dinner under the stars at the camp. Enjoy the sounds of nocturnal wildlife around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at camp before the rhino tracking activity
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the bush or at the conservancy's visitor center café — approx. KES 1,000–1,800
meals.dinner: Bush dinner at camp — approx. KES 2,500–4,000 or included in package

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored, earth-tone clothing for rhino tracking on foot. Avoid bright colors or white. The tracking experience typically lasts 2–3 hours and is moderately active — wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ol Pejeta early and transfer to Amboseli National Park via Nairobi (approx. 5–6 hours total by road, or connect via domestic flight to Amboseli airstrip). Enjoy the changing landscapes as you head south toward Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — arrive and immediately join an afternoon game drive. Africa's largest elephant herds roam Amboseli's open plains with the iconic snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro forming a breathtaking backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at your mid-range Amboseli lodge. Enjoy dinner on the terrace with potential views of Kilimanjaro at sunset — July is one of the best months for clear mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Ol Pejeta before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi or en route — approx. KES 1,200–2,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge — approx. KES 2,500–4,500

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant families are some of the most studied in the world. The Amboseli Elephant Research Project has tracked individual elephants for over 50 years. Ask your guide about specific family groups.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Amboseli National Park at sunrise. This is the golden hour for Kilimanjaro photography — the mountain is clearest in early morning before clouds build. Look for large elephant bulls, lions, cheetahs, and hundreds of bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli observation hill for panoramic views over the swamps and plains. Watch elephants bathing and feeding in the marshes below. Optional: visit a Maasai community near the park boundary for a brief cultural interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge. Enjoy a sundowner cocktail while watching elephants silhouetted against the fading Kilimanjaro skyline — one of Africa's most iconic images.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast during the morning game drive — included or approx. KES 1,000
meals.lunch: Lunch at lodge — approx. KES 1,500–2,500 or included
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge restaurant featuring East African cuisine — approx. KES 2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: 30mm of rain is expected this month — brief afternoon showers are possible but typically short-lived. The rains actually benefit wildlife watching as animals congregate around water sources.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Amboseli early and transfer to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 5–6 hours by road or 1 hour by domestic flight from Amboseli). The Mara is the jewel of Kenya's safari circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — arrive in time for an afternoon game drive. July is peak Great Migration season! Witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles sweeping across the golden Mara plains in one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at your mid-range Mara tented camp. Enjoy a campfire dinner with stories from your guide about the migration patterns and predator activity in the reserve.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch en route or at a roadside stop — approx. KES 1,000–1,500
meals.dinner: Campfire dinner at Mara tented camp — approx. KES 3,000–5,000 or included

day_by_day.notes: July is arguably the best month to visit the Mara — the Great Migration river crossings at the Mara River are at their peak. Ask your guide to position you near the river early for the best chance of witnessing a crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Maasai Mara — early morning game drive at sunrise targeting the famous Mara River crossing points. Position near the river and wait for wildebeest herds to gather and make the dramatic, crocodile-filled crossing. This is a bucket-list wildlife moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Dinner — visit an authentic Maasai village near the Mara. Participate in traditional customs, watch the iconic warrior jumping dance (adumu), learn about Maasai beadwork, and share stories with village elders. This experience provides direct community benefit.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the Maasai village for a special bush dinner set up in the open savannah under a canopy of stars — a magical end to your Mara experience with lanterns, traditional music, and a multi-course meal.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast during the morning game drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at camp or packed picnic on the plains — approx. KES 1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Special bush dinner as part of the Maasai cultural experience — approx. KES 4,000–6,000 or included in experience package

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit is a highlight of any Kenya trip. Bring small gifts such as pens or notebooks for the village school. Bargaining respectfully for beaded jewelry is expected and welcomed. Dress modestly for the village visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara — a last chance to spot the Big Five and soak in the vast golden grasslands. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast and pack up for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Nairobi (approx. 5 hours by road or 45 min by domestic flight). Stop at a reputable craft market such as the Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre in Nairobi for final souvenir shopping — Maasai blankets, wooden carvings, and beaded jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort or a Nairobi hotel for a final night. Celebrate the end of an extraordinary 10-day Kenya adventure with a farewell dinner featuring a mix of Kenyan and international cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final bush breakfast at Mara camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi en route — approx. KES 1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality Nairobi or resort restaurant — approx. KES 3,000–5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and arrange an airport transfer in advance. Kenya Wildlife Service conservation fees are included in most park entry fees. Tip your safari guides and camp staff generously — a standard tip is USD 10–20 per guide per day. This trip covers Kenya's finest wildlife destinations across 10 unforgettable days.

meals.lunch: Light refreshments and welcome canapés provided in the private transfer vehicle
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — a curated 5-course Kenyan coastal tasting menu featuring freshly caught seafood, accompanied by a sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — activities begin only after 13:00. Luggage handling and fast-track immigration assistance arranged in advance. Resort concierge will brief you on the full 10-day itinerary over dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a guided nature walk through the resort's surrounding coastal forest ecosystem. A resident naturalist will introduce you to local bird species, coastal flora, and the unique ecology of Kenya's beachfront environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered light aircraft flight from the nearest airstrip to the Maasai Mara ecosystem — begin your first game drive in the golden afternoon light. Witness large concentrations of wildebeest and zebras beginning the Great Migration crossing preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the open savanna with your private guide, watching elephants and giraffes silhouetted against the Mara sunset. Transfer to your luxury tented camp for the night.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean terrace restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and freshly brewed Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch prepared by the camp chef, served under an acacia tree in the Mara with linen, silverware, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the luxury tented camp's open-air boma — grilled game meats, roasted vegetables, and artisan breads paired with a curated South African wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light safari jacket as evenings in the Mara can be cool (around 16–18°C). Binoculars and camera with telephoto lens highly recommended. All game drives conducted in private 4x4 vehicles with expert Maasai guides.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — drift silently above vast herds of wildebeest and zebras, with sweeping views of the Mara River and surrounding escarpment. A truly once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — afternoon game drive focused on the dramatic Mara River crossing points. Witness millions of wildebeest and zebras braving crocodile-infested waters in one of nature's most spectacular events.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Dinner — visit an authentic Maasai village near the Mara. Participate in traditional warrior jumping ceremonies, learn about beadwork and customs, then enjoy a lavish bush dinner under the stars with traditional storytelling and music.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast served in the bush immediately after the hot air balloon landing — white tablecloth setting with full cooked breakfast, fresh juices, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the luxury tented camp — three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired dishes including nyama choma (roasted meat) and fresh garden salads
meals.dinner: Exclusive bush dinner at the Maasai village — traditional Kenyan cuisine including ugali, sukuma wiki, and slow-roasted meats, elevated with premium ingredients and expert preparation

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon safari departs at approximately 06:00 and lasts around 1.5 hours. Advance booking confirmed. Maasai village visit is conducted with full community consent and benefits the local community directly.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in the Maasai Mara — focus on predator activity as lions, cheetahs, and leopards are most active at dawn. Your expert guide will track fresh prints and signs for an intimate wildlife encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered light aircraft transfer from the Mara airstrip to Amboseli. Upon arrival, afternoon game drive in Amboseli National Park — begin Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views. Observe Africa's largest elephant herds roaming the open plains with the iconic snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive along the Amboseli wetlands, watching elephants bathing and socializing at the swamps as Kilimanjaro glows pink in the fading light. Return to your luxury lodge for a private stargazing session with a resident astronomer.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served at a scenic Mara viewpoint — freshly prepared eggs, pastries, tropical fruits, and premium Kenyan tea and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch served at the Amboseli luxury lodge upon arrival — fresh salads, grilled fish, and artisan breads
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the lodge's signature restaurant — a celebration of Kenyan flavors featuring Amboseli-inspired dishes, with a private table set on the deck overlooking the floodlit waterhole

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli offers some of the best elephant photography in Africa. July skies are typically clear, offering exceptional Kilimanjaro views in the morning and evening. Bring a dust cloth for camera equipment as Amboseli can be dusty.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — morning game drive at first light when Kilimanjaro is most visible and elephant herds gather at the swamps. Your guide will introduce you to specific elephant families tracked by the Amboseli Elephant Research Project.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Elephant Research Project camp for a private briefing with a researcher on elephant behavior, conservation challenges, and the families you observed. Followed by a guided walk (with armed ranger escort) through the Amboseli wetlands.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner experience on a raised platform overlooking the Amboseli plains — watch elephants, zebras, and wildebeest converge at the waterhole as the sun sets behind Kilimanjaro. Champagne and canapés served by your personal butler.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the dawn game drive — continental spread with hot options, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the bush near a shaded acacia grove — gourmet sandwiches, cold cuts, fruit platters, and chilled beverages prepared by the lodge chef
meals.dinner: Seven-course tasting menu at the lodge's exclusive chef's table — Kenyan fusion cuisine with wine pairings selected by the resident sommelier

day_by_day.notes: The Amboseli Elephant Research Project is the world's longest-running elephant study. This exclusive access is a rare privilege. Morning light (06:00–09:00) provides the best conditions for Kilimanjaro photography.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli — final opportunity to photograph elephants with Kilimanjaro at sunrise. Depart by private charter flight to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — afternoon rhino tracking experience on foot and by vehicle. Track both black and white rhinos with expert rangers. Visit the enclosure housing the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — Najin and Fatu — a profoundly moving conservation encounter.
day_by_day.evening: Guided evening game drive in Ol Pejeta — spot lions, leopards, cheetahs, and the conservancy's resident chimpanzee sanctuary. Return to your luxury lodge for a private conservation briefing over cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure — hot buffet with made-to-order eggs, pastries, and fresh tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Ol Pejeta luxury lodge — light Kenyan-inspired dishes featuring locally sourced ingredients from the conservancy
meals.dinner: Exclusive dinner at the lodge's outdoor dining area — a Kenyan barbecue feast featuring premium cuts, accompanied by local wines and traditional live music

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is home to the last two northern white rhinos, Najin and Fatu. This is a deeply significant conservation experience. A portion of your conservancy fees directly funds rhino protection and anti-poaching efforts.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — morning tracking session on foot with expert rangers and trackers. Learn to read animal signs, tracks, and behaviors. Get up-close encounters with both black and white rhinos in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary within Ol Pejeta — the only place in Kenya where you can see chimpanzees. A private guided tour with a primatologist explains the rescue and rehabilitation work. Followed by an afternoon game drive targeting the Big Five.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a scenic Laikipia escarpment viewpoint overlooking Mount Kenya. Return for a private dinner experience under a canopy of stars — the Laikipia plateau offers some of Kenya's most spectacular night skies.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the conservancy — hot coffee, fresh pastries, and a full cooked spread enjoyed with panoramic views of the plains
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the conservancy — artisan sandwiches, antipasto platters, and chilled wines served on a private blanket spread
meals.dinner: Private starlight dinner in the conservancy — a romantic 6-course meal served under the stars with ambient lantern lighting and live acoustic guitar

day_by_day.notes: Morning rhino tracking requires moderate fitness as some walking on uneven terrain is involved. Comfortable closed-toe shoes and neutral-colored clothing recommended. The northern white rhino encounter is a once-in-a-generation experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru. Morning arrival and immediate game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari, witnessing hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos carpeting the lake shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continued Lake Nakuru safari — explore the park's diverse habitats including acacia woodlands and rocky escarpments. Spot Rothschild's giraffes (one of Africa's rarest subspecies), white rhinos, lions, leopards, and over 450 bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat excursion on Lake Nakuru (where accessible) to view flamingos and pelicans from the water. Return to your luxury lodge perched on the escarpment with panoramic views over the lake, glowing pink with flamingos in the fading light.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Ol Pejeta lodge before departure — full hot breakfast with freshly baked breads and Kenyan specialty teas
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch at the Lake Nakuru luxury lodge — fresh lake fish (tilapia), seasonal vegetables, and artisan salads with a view over the flamingo-studded lake
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner on the lodge's private escarpment terrace — a curated menu of Kenyan and East African specialties with panoramic night views of Lake Nakuru

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo population fluctuates with water levels and algae blooms — July typically offers excellent flamingo viewing. The park is also one of Kenya's best spots for rhino sightings. Binoculars essential for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the Lake Nakuru shoreline with a specialist ornithologist — identify rare and endemic species including the African fish eagle, goliath heron, and greater flamingo. Photography session during the golden hour when flamingo colors are most vivid.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight back to the Nairobi area, then onward transfer to the coast. Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's private beach, infinity pool, and luxury spa facilities. Optional deep-tissue or traditional Kenyan massage at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail reception at the resort's beachfront bar — watch the Indian Ocean sunset over Champagne and premium canapés. Reflect on the extraordinary wildlife experiences of the past week.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge — fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and a full cooked breakfast before the morning walk
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon return — fresh seafood, salads, and cold-pressed juices by the pool
meals.dinner: Gourmet seafood dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — whole grilled lobster, Swahili-spiced prawns, and catch-of-the-day preparations with fine wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The return journey via charter flight ensures a comfortable and scenic transfer. The resort spa offers traditional Kenyan treatments using locally sourced ingredients including baobab oil and Kenyan honey — advance booking recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure at the Aegean Bliss Resort — sunrise yoga session on the private beach led by the resort's wellness instructor. Last swim in the Indian Ocean and a final stroll along the beachfront to soak in the coastal atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at the resort followed by private luxury transfer to Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. En route, stop at a premium curio shop for last-minute authentic Kenyan souvenirs — Maasai beadwork, carved wooden sculptures, and specialty Kenyan coffee and tea.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Access to the airport's premium VIP lounge with à la carte dining, premium bar, and shower facilities. Board your return flight with extraordinary memories of Kenya's wildlife, landscapes, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final luxury breakfast at the resort's ocean terrace — a grand spread of tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, eggs any style, smoked fish, and specialty Kenyan single-origin pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the resort's signature restaurant — a curated 4-course menu celebrating the best of Kenyan coastal cuisine, with a complimentary glass of vintage Champagne
meals.dinner: Premium dining in the VIP airport lounge — à la carte Kenyan and international dishes, fine wines, and specialty cocktails before departure

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at the resort is 12:00 — late check-out until 14:00 can be arranged subject to availability. Ensure all souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no wildlife products, ivory, or live animals. Your concierge will assist with any last-minute arrangements or gift wrapping.
